concepts.title: Crisis of 1991 and the New Economic Policy LPG
concepts.definition: The balance of payments crisis of 1991, with dwindling foreign exchange reserves and heavy external debt, forced India to adopt the New Economic Policy of stabilisation and structural reform in three streams: liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation.
concepts.key_idea: Reforms dismantled the licensing raj, opened sectors to private and foreign investment, and integrated India with the world economy.

solution_steps.explain: Recall the 1991 reserves crisis and IMF loan conditions.
Place each measure under L, P or G.
Link the measure to efficiency, growth or integration.

concepts.title: Liberalisation: Deregulation of Industry, Finance, Trade and Tax
concepts.definition: Liberalisation freed economic activity from state controls by abolishing industrial licensing for most industries, deregulating the financial sector, reducing tariffs and removing quantitative restrictions on imports, and reforming direct and indirect taxes to simplify compliance.
concepts.key_idea: Freedom of production, trade and finance was expected to let market prices allocate resources better than licences and controls.

solution_steps.explain: Separate industry, finance, trade and tax reforms.
State which control or restriction was lifted.

concepts.title: Privatisation, Globalisation and Demonetisation GST Context
concepts.definition: Privatisation transfers ownership or management from the public to the private sector through disinvestment of equity of public sector undertakings, while globalisation integrates the domestic economy with the world through trade liberalisation, foreign direct investment inflows and outward orientation of policy.
concepts.key_idea: Disinvestment sales of PSU equity aimed to raise resources and improve efficiency, and globalisation opened the economy to foreign competition and technology.

solution_steps.explain: Distinguish ownership transfer from world integration.

State gains and concerns of each measure.

concepts.title: Appraisal of Reforms: Gains, Critique and Positive Features
concepts.definition: Reforms raised growth of the economy and foreign exchange reserves and expanded the service sector, but critics note limited employment growth, neglect of agriculture, uneven industrial growth and greater inequality, while positive assessments emphasise efficiency and consumer gains.
concepts.key_idea: The reform appraisal weighs faster GDP growth and reserves against jobless growth and agrarian neglect.

solution_steps.explain: Note growth, reserves and efficiency improvements.

Weigh gains against concerns for a conclusion.
